REPOSITORY: https://github.com/Joedge-Vasconcelos/tequantum

Summary

TE-QUANTUM is an integrated universal quantum simulation and AI ecosystem that combines advanced physical modeling, exact algebraic computing, and space agency datasets to accelerate research in quantum nanotechnology, energy conversion, and planetary exploration. Unlike siloed simulation tools, the platform unifies real-time quantum circuit execution, 2D CdTe quantum well compilers, 3D WebGL nanoparticle observatories, and direct orbital telemetry from NASA, ESA, and CSA missions. A central feature of the platform is the identification of locations on Earth that serve as analogues for permanent base locations on the Moon and Mars environments. Powered by the TEC-OÑ physical medium and 2Ñ KET architecture, the system allows researchers and students to calculate thermoelectric parameters, simulate quantum entanglements, analyze lunar and Martian analogues, and explore exoplanet transit curves. Scientific results and workflows are delivered through an accessible web portal with live AI equation runners, CSV/JSON telemetry exports, and interactive educational games.

Project Details

TE-QUANTUM (TEC-OÑ | 2Ñ Qubits) is a comprehensive full-stack platform designed to provide unrestricted access to cutting-edge physics technologies and universal applications. Built upon 2Ñ Qubits from the original TEC-OÑ model featuring 1,098 connections and delivering a minimum efficiency 1,444 times higher than the predecessor technology of the same purpose in the global sector, the TEC-OÑ ecosystem is applied in more than 130 institutions, including more than 100 research laboratories, industrial centers, and quantum computers, with equations validated in cooperation with large research centers such as CNPEM and UNICAMP.

The platform integrates several specialized modules such as:

*AI and Universal Equation Compilers: Features live TEQuantum Executor AI, TEC-OÑ Oracle, custom GPT compilers, and the 2Ñ Chain Rule algorithm that links numeric sets and dimensional quantities.

*Quantum Physics and Nanotechnology Simulators: Includes a real-time 2D CdTe Quantum Simulator that calculates Seebeck coefficients, energy levels demonstrating quantum yield without violating the second law of thermodynamics, a 3D WebGL Quantum Observatory for core-shell nanoparticles including wave functions and Brus curves, and the Brazilian Quantum Platform KET (2Ñ) to simulate CNOT quantum gates.

*Integration of aerospace and NASA/ESA data (lunar and Martian analogues): Connects directly to NASA Worldview, Earthdata Search, PDS Geosciences including LRO, Diviner, and Mars Trek, CSA Radar SAR, ESA Copernicus, and NandITESS.ai. This includes a dedicated solution for identifying and scoring Earth locations analogous to permanent lunar base locations using LRO, Diviner, and LOLA datasets and Mars environments using PDS, CRISM, and SHARAD datasets, while also integrating Earthdata Search and the CSA RCM and RADARSAT-1 radar.

*Interactive Quantum Games and Gamification: Combines exact science with engagement through three interactive experiences including TE-QUANTUM.IO as a space arena, Quantum Tycoon expanding the 859-unit national research network, and Sekai Deluxe as a 6-chapter narrative arcade.

The project stands out for its creative fusion of rigorous quantum physics, aerospace data science, and interactive gamification. By combining professional R&D tools, such as direct exports of CSV and JSON datasets, with intuitive 3D visualizations, terrestrial-to-planetary analog tagging, and educational games, TE-QUANTUM transforms complex quantum mechanics and astrophysics into an interactive, reproducible, and engaging experience.
